newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda doubles number of village police.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda doubles number of village police.

text.p: Rwanda doubled the size of its village police force on Sunday amid mounting insecurity, holding a graduation ceremony for 750 policemen trained by foreign experts.
The force of 1,500 men is assigned to local communes to prevent crime on a day-to-day basis, track down criminals, and guard local jails.
"These are community police who have to live with the people and help them," their commander, Denis Karera, said.

The first 750 men graduated from the Gishari school, 130 km (80 miles) east of the capital Kigali, nearly a year ago. Although the force is to be expanded to 3,000 within a year, it will be small compared to Rwandas 40,000-strong regular police force.

Rwandan officials say keeping law and order is a tremendeous task after the 1994 genocide in which up to 800,000 minority Tutsis and allied Hutus were massacred. Many members of the former communal police took part in the genocide and fled into exile to escape retribution.
Insecurity in Rwanda has increased in the last two months, with hundreds of killings reported following the return of a million mostly Hutu refugees from neighbouring countries.
Government and army officials blame the fresh killings on returning Hutu extremists.

"Watch out for criminal groups. Make it impossible for them to operate," training camp commander Geeorge Rumanzi told the new police parading in neat blue uniforms and peaked caps. The communal police have access to firearms, but do not normally carry them.
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has co-ordinated technical assistance for the force, with support from Britain, the United States and other Western countries.
